Tenaris has invested over $240 million USD in oilfield services in Argentina, providing hydraulic fracturing equipment and a third coiled tubing unit that work systematically in well conditions.


Tenaris


**Andrea Previtali** , Tenaris President for the Southern Cone, recently participated in an oilfield services companies CEOs panel alongside representatives of Calfrac, Halliburton and SLB at AOG Patagonia 2026, sharing the growth of Tenaris’s oilfield services industry in Argentina, launched just six years ago, and the company’s next steps.


Tenaris has invested more than $240 million USD in oilfield services in Argentina in recent years. In Vaca Muerta, one of the world's largest shale oil and gas reservoirs, Tenaris’s oilfield services division provides hydraulic fracturing equipment, which stimulates wells so they can produce. The company recently added a third fracturing set with Dynamic Gas Blending (DGB) Tier IV technology, which uses compressed natural gas as a power source to reduce diesel consumption.


The division also added a third coiled tubing unit, equipment that works inside wells using continuous flexible steel tubing. In early 2027, Tenaris will start a turnkey service for building the surface casing, the first section of the well. By applying the company’s extensive pipe production experience, the equipment now exceeds 22 pumping hours per day. "As productivity increases, fewer fracturing sets are needed for the same production," Previtali explained.


That focus on turning industrial know-how into valuable solutions for customers is also what led Tenaris to offer its integrated solution for building the surface casing. Tenaris provides the rig, casing, bit, cement and fluids, and delivers the casing installed and cemented, validated to each operator's quality controls.


Previtali also described education as a founding value of the company: "When we talk about industry, we cannot forget about education," he said, adding that more than 90% of Tenaris's community relations budget goes to educational initiatives. The Roberto Rocca Scholarships, run by Tenaris and its sister companies in the Techint Group, is celebrating its 50th anniversary. The program reaches 23 countries and has awarded more than 45,000 scholarships. In Neuquén, Tenaris also supports Tecpetrol-led initiatives for final-year students of the province's technical schools.
